en.title: Maximum Order Volume
en.description:
A supermarket receives n calls in one day. Each call has a start time start, a duration duration, and an order volume volume. Choose non-conflicting calls to maximize the total order volume. Following the source's implementations in three languages, call intervals are half-open [start, start+duration): when one call ends exactly when the next one starts, both calls can be taken back to back.

Original constraints: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤start[i], duration[i], volume[i]≤10^9.

Original source: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/snowflake#11-maximum-order-volume-weighted-interval-scheduling (fixed snapshot content fingerprint 0c74f501c9c27779e35805b2c9ac24588e2d0ca5c2b84f5ed60def2c9c34468f).
en.input: The first line contains n; the next three lines contain the n values of start, duration, and volume, respectively.
en.output: Output the maximum total order volume that can be obtained.
en.explanation: Sort by end time. Let dp[i] be the maximum order volume using the first i calls; when choosing call i, binary search for the number p of calls whose end time is no later than its start time, and the transition is max(dp[i-1], dp[p]+volume[i]).
hints: Sort the calls by end time.
Before choosing the current call, binary search for the last call that can come right before it.
